theory.overview: Backtracking is a systematic way of trying out different sequences of decisions until a solution is found. It builds candidates incrementally and abandons a candidate ('backtracks') as soon as it determines the candidate cannot possibly lead to a valid solution. Think of it as a refined brute force that prunes invalid branches early. Classic applications include N-Queens, Sudoku, permutation generation, and constraint satisfaction problems.

keyConcepts.name: State Space Tree
keyConcepts.description: Visualize all possible solutions as a tree. Each level represents a decision, each branch a choice. Search this tree depth-first.

keyConcepts.name: Pruning
keyConcepts.description: Abandon partial candidates when they violate constraints. Reduces exponential search space dramatically.

keyConcepts.name: Constraint Propagation
keyConcepts.description: After each choice, propagate constraints to reduce future choices. Used in Sudoku solvers and constraint satisfaction.

keyConcepts.name: Heuristics
keyConcepts.description: Most Constrained Variable: choose variable with fewest valid options first. Least Constraining Value: choose value that rules out fewest options.

complexity.space: O(d) for recursion stack where d is depth

problems.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets

algorithmSteps.description: 3-Queens: Empty 3x3 board. Place 3 queens so none attack each other.
Place queen at (0,0). Mark row 0, col 0, diagonals.
Row 1, Col 0: Invalid - same diagonal as (0,0).
Row 2: No valid positions! Backtrack - remove queen from (1,2).
Row 1, Col 1: Invalid - same diagonal as (0,0). Try next.

minigame.title: N-Queens Puzzle
minigame.description: Place N queens on N×N board so no two attack each other. Watch backtracking in action as it tries, fails, and backtracks.
